summary: Iteration 6 testing complete. Boombox redesign verified end-to-end. The graffiti boombox photo (qdcx3gp4) is correctly used as the body with interactive percentage-positioned overlays. All 8 hotspot buttons (prev/play/pause/stop/next/rec/volume/power) work. Play swaps to pause and starts audio (LCD time advances from 00:00 to 00:02+ within 2.5s). Deck A reels spin during playback (verified animate-spin class). Cassette reels use the new 6-spoke diamond clip-path (polygon(50% 0%, 100% 50%, 50% 100%, 0% 50%)) — NOT circular CD-style. Next/Prev cycle tracks. Volume cycles (75 -> 100 confirmed) with toast. Power OFF shows '— OFF —' on LCD, clicking play while off shows 'Boombox is off. Hit the power switch.' toast. Power ON restores LCD. Free download via track-row 'Free DL' button triggers REC LED on Deck B, deck-b reels spin (yellow), and REC LED disappears after ~4s. deck-a-click surface triggers play. Backend smoke: GET /api/instrumentals returns 7 tracks, POST /api/instrumentals/free-starter-01/download returns audio_url + downloads counter. 14/14 backend tests pass. Zero console errors observed.

issues: Visually, the LCD bar (top:40.2%) and cassette reels (top:47%) sit on top of the photo's painted tuner/cassette area but they don't fully cover the underlying graffiti-painted cassette labels (BEATS/DEZ are still visible behind the 6-spoke reels). This is acceptable but the reels look small relative to the cassette wells. Consider increasing reel width or making them more opaque so they read as 'real' cassette spools rather than overlay decoration.

Transport button hotspots (top:65.5%) are large translucent circles positioned over the chrome button row in the photo. They are visually obvious as overlays — the chrome buttons in the photo are still visible behind. Not a bug, but the overlay aesthetic competes with the photo. Consider lower default opacity (e.g. border-white/20 bg-black/20) when not hovered.
Power ON/OFF text label and volume number sit in tiny 4% x 4.5% buttons at top-left — on smaller viewports the text becomes hard to read (text-[7px]).

critical_code_review_comments: Boombox.jsx useEffect at line 86 depends on isPlaying and powered but does not include them in its deps array — ESLint exhaustive-deps would flag this. Currently harmless because state changes trigger re-render with fresh refs but should be cleaned up.

handleDownload (line 148) uses a hardcoded 4000ms setTimeout to fake the 'recording' duration. This works visually but is decoupled from the real download progress. Acceptable as a visual flourish; document intent in a code comment.

togglePower toast logic at line 179 reads `toast(powered ? 'Power OFF' : 'Power ON')` but it runs BEFORE the state update fully commits — the closure reads the OLD `powered` value, which actually works out correctly (saying OFF when transitioning ON->OFF). Code is correct but counter-intuitive; consider computing the next value once and using it in both setPowered and toast for clarity.

The boombox container is aspect-square and the photo is rendered with object-cover — on extremely wide or narrow viewports the photo may crop, shifting the painted controls relative to the percentage overlays. The current max-w-4xl + aspect-square keeps it stable on desktop and tablet, but verify on very small mobile screens (<360px) where the 4% wide power/volume buttons become <14px tap targets (below WCAG 24px min).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (31/31 assertions across image, hotspots, play/pause swap, lcd advance, reel spin/clip-path, next/prev, volume cycle, power off+toast, power on, download REC LED + deck-b spin + auto-clear, deck-a-click play)
